# Water Capital Wire

> A free daily read on the business of water for managers, investors and operators: capital, companies, technology, infrastructure and water security, with every fact sourced and dated. Each edition has a lead story traced through the water cycle (source, treatment, use, reuse, discharge), briefs across the water economy, weekly spotlights on a company, a leader, a supplier, an innovation and an investor, a capital desk of deals and firms, a water atlas on stress, demand, infrastructure, emerging sectors and security, a watchlist of water equities, a project calculator and an events calendar. General information, not investment advice.

## Today's edition
- [Durham has paid over $4 million for borrowed water as North Carolina's drought reaches 6.2 million people](https://watercapitalwire.com/): November 22, 2026. North Carolina's drought now reaches 6.2 million people. Durham had 76 days of easily accessible water on November 17 and has paid more than $4 million for 898 million gallons bought from Cary and OWASA, because it has no plant of its own on Jordan Lake.
- [Capital: American Water tells staff merger planning with Essential is largely complete](https://watercapitalwire.com/#money)
- [Utilities: Thames Water's plan to push £12 billion of debt to 2028 goes to court on November 27](https://watercapitalwire.com/#world)
- [Regulation: EWG's tap water update finds chromium-6 in water serving more than 260 million Americans](https://watercapitalwire.com/#contaminants)
- [Technology: Ecolab pilots zero wastewater discharge at chip plants and plans to bring it to India](https://watercapitalwire.com/#chips)
- [Desalination: Veolia wins nearly €200 million in Gulf desalination work](https://watercapitalwire.com/#desal)
